history.sg_progress: The Peacebuilding Fund is pursuing its funding plan as set out in its strategy for the period 2020–2024. The Secretary-General hosted a high-level replenishment conference in January 2021, which expanded the donor base. The Peacebuilding Support Office is following up with a range of long-standing and new donors to ensure that pledges are implemented and to continue to expand the donor base. This complements the ongoing Member State-led dialogue at the General Assembly and the Peacebuilding Commission on financing for peacebuilding.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration develop a more comprehensive financing plan and expand the donor base to achieve funding targets.
history.administration_response: The Peacebuilding Fund has developed a resource mobilization plan for 2022, which was presented at the Advisory Group meeting of March 2022. This plan sets out ways in which the financing of the Fund could be better shared among Member States. In addition, the Secretary-General has presented a proposal to the Fifth Committee to use assessed contributions to finance a core portion of the Fund, amounting to $100 million, on an annual basis. This proposal would significantly expand the donor base to all Member States.
history.board_assessment: Given that the Peacebuilding Support Office in the Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs did not meet the target of annual financial contributions to the Peacebuilding Fund in 2021, the Board consider this recommendation to be under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration develop a more comprehensive financing plan and expand the donor base in order to achieve funding targets.
history.administration_response: The decision of the General Assembly in its resolution 78/257 in December 2023 to provide assessed contributions to the Peacebuilding Fund represents a landmark decision that will bring more predictable and sustainable resources while underscoring that peacebuilding is at the core of the work of the United Nations in which all Member States are committed to investing. Starting from 2025, $50 million will be provided annually, earmarked for the Fund’s Peacebuilding and Recovery Facility in specified countries and territories. Member States, in particular through the Peacebuilding Commission and the Secretary-General’s Peacebuilding Fund Advisory Group, will be consulted on allocations. The Administration therefore requests closure of this recommendation.
history.board_assessment: Given that a more comprehensive plan has been established, the Board considers this recommendation to be implemented.
